criteria.criterion: A single shared helper exists that writes script bytes by spawning a child process (sh with bytes on stdin: cat to a tmp file, chmod 755, mv into place) and waits for it; the test process never opens the script for writing. Confirm by reading it.
criteria.evidence: Read crates/athena-git/src/script_writer.rs. `write_executable(path, bytes)` spawns `sh -c 'cat > "$1.writing" && chmod 755 "$1.writing" && mv "$1.writing" "$1"'` with stdin piped, writes the bytes to the pipe, drops it, then calls `child.wait()` and asserts success. The calling process never opens the script path. The module doc explains ETXTBSY and why a child does the writing. It is exported as `pub mod script_writer` in athena-git/src/lib.rs.

criteria.criterion: Every test in the workspace that writes a file and then makes it executable (set_permissions, from_mode, set_mode, xtask set_executable, or an external chmod) calls the helper. This covers at least reading.rs, checks.rs, claude.rs, reconcile.rs, athena-git snapshot.rs and the xtask tests. Grep of test code finds no remaining write-then-chmod pairs. Production set_executable uses are untouched.
criteria.evidence: Grep of all *.rs files for set_permissions|from_mode|set_mode|set_executable|chmod, and for 0o7xx|.mode(|+x|PermissionsExt|#!/bin/sh. The only remaining hits are production code (toolconfig.rs, pin.rs, core snapshot.rs, athena-git snapshot.rs set_mode/restore, xtask set_executable at lines 415/490/550/807), chmod used as a policy string (policy.rs, cap-change lib.rs), and read-only mode assertions (pin.rs:650, athena-git snapshot.rs:537). The diff converts reading.rs stub_binary, checks.rs a_cargo_test_check_records_its_failing_tests_and_the_flag_it_ran_with, claude.rs stand_in, reconcile.rs world() (the fake gh), athena-git snapshot.rs user_repo, and xtask stand_in_claude and a_cached_gitleaks_is_skipped_only_when_it_reports_the_pinned_version. The diff does not touch production set_executable.

criteria.criterion: A stress test runs many write-then-exec cycles through the helper while other threads fork, and asserts every exec succeeds.
criteria.evidence: `many_write_then_exec_cycles_succeed_while_other_threads_fork` in script_writer.rs: 4 forker threads loop `Command::new("true")` while 4 writer threads each do 100 cycles of write_executable then exec. Each exec is checked: it must spawn (panic otherwise), exit successfully, and print the expected stdout.

findings.summary: The test-only helper ships as a public module of the production athena-git library, with no feature gate.
findings.evidence: `pub mod script_writer;` has no cfg or feature gate, so every production build of athena-git exports a panicking test utility. The reading suggested a `test-support` feature, which would keep it out of the production API. It works as is.

findings.summary: The stress test has no control run showing that a direct write followed by chmod fails under the same forking load.
findings.evidence: The test shows the helper survives 400 cycles under concurrent forks. It never shows the old pattern failing, so it cannot tell a fixed race apart from a race that did not happen in this run. The race is probabilistic, so a control would be flaky; this is acceptable but worth noting.

findings.summary: The test-only retry in reading.rs check_stub is now redundant, and its doc comment describes a busy stub that can no longer occur.
findings.evidence: The comment says "trying again while the freshly written stub is busy (a parallel test's fork can hold it)". stub_binary now writes through the helper. The brief allowed removing test-only retry code made redundant, but did not require it.
The fixture list writes "#!/bin/sh\necho hi\n", then write_executable rewrites the same bytes. The behavior is correct; the content is just duplicated.

summary: The change does what was asked. It adds `athena_git::script_writer::write_executable`, which writes a script through a short-lived `sh` child (cat to a temp file, chmod 755, mv into place) and waits for it, so the test process never holds the script open for writing. All 7 test sites that wrote a file and then made it executable now use it. I grepped every .rs file and found no remaining write-then-chmod pair in test code; the only other hits are production code (left alone) or policy strings. The stress test runs 400 write-then-exec cycles while four threads fork. It passed when I ran it, as did every converted test. The new D157 entry and its `amended` link (line 4319) satisfy D156, and the decision-log tests (the decisions lib tests and the backtest file) pass. No new test file was added, so shard-timings.txt is unchanged. The CHANGELOG lists each converted site and matches the diff. The job report itself is not in my snapshot. Every changed file is on the deliverables list. For the whole workspace I cited Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test passes. The four findings are all minor or nits: the helper is a public, ungated module of the production athena-git crate; the stress test has no control run of the old pattern; a test-only retry in reading.rs is now redundant; and one fixture writes run.sh twice. Verdict: pass.
